title: Implicit Preference Alignment for Human Image Animation
claim: Standard preference optimization needs both good and bad samples; ours drops the bad-sample requirement and aligns using only good ones.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right pipeline, dashed box marks the discarded bad samples
description: A single wide left-to-right flow diagram. On the far left are a reference image and a pose sequence. Both feed into a blue frozen pretrained generation model, marked with a snowflake. Its output goes through a human preference annotation icon, a head with gears. This splits into a stack of good-sample frames with a thumbs-up and a stack of bad-sample frames with a thumbs-down. Both stacks show a woman with red boxes around her hands. The bad samples sit inside a gray dashed rounded box with a gray X, which signals that they are unnecessary. A large arrow labeled Human Preference Alignment leads to the right. There, an orange trainable Aligned Generation Model, marked with a flame, sits above a frozen blue pretrained model. Both take image and pose inputs. Dashed curved arrows connect the models to a loss formula, L = -log sigma(beta Delta(p_ref, p_theta)). The eye goes first to the photos and the crossed-out bad-sample box.
caption: Overview of the Implicit Preference Alignment (IPA) framework for enhancing hand generation quality. IPA eliminates the necessity for bad samples inherent in standard preference optimization frameworks (e.g., direct preference optimization), alleviating the burden for preference annotation. We have also theoretically proved in Sec. [ref] that IPA inherently performs implicit reward maximization.
abstract: Human image animation has witnessed significant advancements, yet generating high-fidelity hand motions remains a persistent challenge due to their high degrees of freedom and motion complexity. While reinforcement learning from human feedback, particularly direct preference optimization, offers a potential solution, it necessitates the construction of strict preference pairs. However, curating such pairs for dynamic hand regions is prohibitively expensive and often impractical due to frame-wise inconsistencies. In this paper, we propose Implicit Preference Alignment (IPA), a data-efficient post-training framework that eliminates the need for paired preference data. Theoretically grounded in implicit reward maximization, IPA aligns the model by maximizing the likelihood of self-generated high-quality samples while penalizing deviations from the pretrained prior. Furthermore, we introduce a Hand-Aware Local Optimization mechanism to explicitly steer the alignment process toward hand regions. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves effective preference optimization to enhance hand generation quality, while significantly lowering the barrier for constructing preference data. Codes are released at https://github.com/mdswyz/IPA
